canonical_statement: The review summarizes pharmacologic treatment of acute cluster attacks, transitional therapy, and preventive therapy; neurostimulation is outside its scope.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This review summarizes drug therapy of cluster attacks and prophylactic treatment. Neurostimulation methods are not addressed.

canonical_statement: Preventive treatment recommendations are constrained by very few placebo-controlled studies and are often based on open observational evidence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: there are unfortunately very few placebo-controlled studies. Therefore, most treatment recommendations are limited to results from open observational studies.

canonical_statement: Because cluster attacks typically last 15-180 minutes, the review does not recommend oral medication for aborting individual attacks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The individual cluster attacks are rather short and between 15 and 180 min. Therefore, oral medication is not recommended.

canonical_statement: The review identifies 100% oxygen, subcutaneous sumatriptan, intranasal sumatriptan, and intranasal zolmitriptan as principal acute pharmacologic options.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The cluster attacks are treated with subcutaneous sumatriptan or triptans as nasal sprays. An effective therapy is oxygen inhalation using a rebreather mask.

canonical_statement: In a cited randomized placebo-controlled trial of 39 patients, 74% achieved freedom from pain or almost complete relief at 15 minutes with subcutaneous sumatriptan 6 mg versus 26% with placebo.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This endpoint [15 min] was achieved in 74% of the patients treated with sumatriptan and 26% for placebo.

population.label: Patients in cited randomized placebo-controlled acute cluster headache trial

concept.text: Freedom from pain or almost complete relief

canonical_statement: In the same cited trial, pain freedom at 10 minutes occurred in 36% with subcutaneous sumatriptan 6 mg versus 3% with placebo.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The success rate of 6 mg of sumatriptan subcutaneously for pain free at 10 min was 36% and for placebo 3%.

population.label: Patients in cited randomized placebo-controlled acute cluster headache trial

canonical_statement: A cited Cochrane pooled analysis reported pain freedom at 15 minutes in 48% with sumatriptan versus 17% with placebo, with NNT 3.3 (95% CI 2.4-5.0).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: pain-free results after 15 min for 48% with sumatriptan and 17% with placebo, resulting in a number needed to treat of 3.3 (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.4–5.0).

population.label: Participants in cited pooled acute cluster headache trials

canonical_statement: In a cited randomized double-blind trial of 118 patients treating 154 attacks, 30-minute headache response occurred in 57% with intranasal sumatriptan 20 mg versus 26% with placebo (p=0.002).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The responder rates at 30 min were 57% for sumatriptan and 26% for placebo (p = 0.002).

population.label: Patients in cited intranasal sumatriptan trial

outcome.definition: Decrease from very severe, severe, or moderate pain to mild or no pain

canonical_statement: In that cited trial, pain freedom at 30 minutes occurred in 47% with intranasal sumatriptan 20 mg versus 18% with placebo (p=0.003).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Pain-free rates at 30 min were 47% for sumatriptan and 18% for placebo (p = 0.003).

population.label: Patients in cited intranasal sumatriptan trial

population.label: Patients in cited intranasal sumatriptan trial

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In conclusion, only preventive therapy with verapamil and lithium has evidence from randomized studies.
